title: HYDE · Operations
description: Day-to-day health of the charging lab for the operations team: backend and charger connectivity, freshness of charger reports, session and connection churn, command outcomes, faults with their matching log lines, per-gun service state and the buffer battery. Truth-first: 'No data' means nothing was reported (only counts are zero-filled), sessions are ordered by time (never by transaction id, which resets on redeploys), and in-progress sessions are never given a final verdict. Times display in your browser's timezone (site local time is Central European, CEST). Alert rules live in the Grafana folder 'OCPP Lab' — link at the bottom. Mode switch: the `mode` variable separates Live hardware from simulators everywhere. Prometheus panels in Live/Simulation cover data from the deploy that introduced the mode label (2026-07-21) onward — older series show only under All. Timescale-backed panels split across ALL history (backfilled).

list.description: Global data mode. Live = real hardware on the LIVE_CHARGER_IDS allowlist; Simulation = every other charge-point id (internal sim, EXT01, test rigs); All = both. Prometheus series recorded before the mode label existed (pre 2026-07-21) only appear under All; Timescale history is backfilled and splits correctly.

options.content:
HYDE OPERATIONS
Service health · faults · commands · buffer battery

panels.title: Backend
panels.description: Whether the OCPP central system’s metrics endpoint answered its latest scrape (every 5 s). DOWN means the backend process is unreachable — chargers cannot start or stop sessions while it is down.

panels.title: Chargers online
panels.description: Chargers holding a live websocket to the backend right now. Guarded by the scrape state: if the backend is unreachable this shows 'backend unreachable' rather than a stale count.

panels.title: Chargers online — over time
panels.description: Connected-charger count over the selected range. Gaps mean the backend was not scrapeable at that time (unknown state) — they are deliberately not drawn as zero.

panels.title: Charger freshness — newest report per charger
panels.description: Newest stored data report of any kind per charger, all time. The real charger (A2111…) reports its buffer battery roughly every 15 minutes even when idle, so more than ~35 minutes of silence while it shows as online is suspicious (amber text), and hours of silence are red text. chargePointSim and EXT01 are software test rigs that only report during test sessions — long silence there is expected.

targets.rawSql: SELECT charge_point AS "charge point", max(ts) AS "last report", EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (now() - max(ts))) AS "silent for" FROM meter_samples WHERE (CASE WHEN '$mode' = 'live' THEN NOT is_sim WHEN '$mode' = 'sim' THEN is_sim ELSE true END) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: Connections & sessions per minute
panels.description: Charger socket churn (connections opened/closed) and charging session starts/stops, per minute. Spiky open/close pairs without sessions usually mean network trouble — Cloudflare idle cuts or a charger reboot loop. rate() runs over $__rate_interval with a 5 s min step so short-lived churn shows at its true height.

panels.title: Command success
panels.description: Share of operator commands (remote start/stop, unlock, configuration, …) the chargers answered positively in the selected range — counted as Accepted / Unlocked / Scheduled / RebootRequired responses. 'No commands in range' is the truth when nothing was sent, not an error.

panels.title: Command results by status (per min)
panels.description: Every command response from the chargers, broken down by the status they answered (Accepted, Rejected, NotSupported, …). Empty panel = no commands were sent in the range. Finish-palette rule: bronze is excluded from the categorical rotation on any panel where alert-red can appear (fault codes, command statuses) — fallback order Silver → Steel → Graphite; burgundy (unused today) requires a CVD check against alert-red before ever appearing near alerts.

panels.title: Charger faults
panels.description: Fault reports (status notifications carrying an error code) received from chargers in the selected range. Zero-filled deliberately: zero faults is a real, meaningful zero.

panels.title: Faults by error code (per min)
panels.description: Charger fault reports broken down by their error code. The vendor-specific detail code, when a charger sends one, is visible in the matching log line on the right. Known codes wear the neutral finish palette; a code not seen before renders alert-red until classified. Finish-palette rule: bronze is excluded from the categorical rotation on any panel where alert-red can appear (fault codes, command statuses) — fallback order Silver → Steel → Graphite; burgundy (unused today) requires a CVD check against alert-red before ever appearing near alerts.

panels.title: Errors & charger fault lines (backend log)
panels.description:
Backend log lines at warn/error severity plus charger status lines mentioning a fault — the place to find vendor error details (open a line for its full metadata, including the reporting charger). The recurring harmless 'upgrade failed' probe noise (health checks and scanners hitting the websocket port) is filtered out here; the unfiltered stream lives on the OCPP Registry dashboard.

Mode filter: charger-attributed log lines follow the Live/Simulation switch; infrastructure lines (no charger id) always show.

panels.title: Guns in service
panels.description: Per-gun service picture. 'last report' is the newest stored data of any kind (idle buffer-battery reports included, all time); 'last session' is the newest session end ever; 'sessions' and 'kWh' count only the dashboard's time range (default 24 h). A blank kWh means the gun reported no import energy meter in range (true for the software test rigs) — blank is the truth there, not zero. Reused transaction ids (the lab backend's counter resets on redeploy) are split into separate sessions by a 15-minute quiet gap.

targets.rawSql: WITH samp AS (SELECT charge_point, connector_id, transaction_id, ts, measurand, unit, value, CASE WHEN ts - lag(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY charge_point, connector_id, transaction_id ORDER BY ts) > interval '15 minutes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS new_seg FROM meter_samples WHERE (CASE WHEN '$mode' = 'live' THEN NOT is_sim WHEN '$mode' = 'sim' THEN is_sim ELSE true END) AND transaction_id IS NOT NULL), seg AS (SELECT *, sum(new_seg) OVER (PARTITION BY charge_point, connector_id, transaction_id ORDER BY ts ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS seg_no FROM samp), seg2 AS (SELECT *, max(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY charge_point, connector_id, transaction_id, seg_no) AS seg_end FROM seg), sessions AS (SELECT charge_point, connector_id, transaction_id, seg_no, min(ts) AS start_ts, max(ts) AS end_ts, EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (max(ts) - min(ts))) AS dur_s, COALESCE(max(value * CASE WHEN unit = 'kWh' THEN 1 WHEN unit = 'MWh' THEN 1000 ELSE 0.001 END) FILTER (WHERE measurand = 'Energy.Active.Import.Register') - min(value * CASE WHEN unit = 'kWh' THEN 1 WHEN unit = 'MWh' THEN 1000 ELSE 0.001 END) FILTER (WHERE measurand = 'Energy.Active.Import.Register'), max(value * CASE WHEN unit = 'kWh' THEN 1 WHEN unit = 'MWh' THEN 1000 ELSE 0.001 END) FILTER (WHERE measurand LIKE 'Energy.Active.%.Register') - min(value * CASE WHEN unit = 'kWh' THEN 1 WHEN unit = 'MWh' THEN 1000 ELSE 0.001 END) FILTER (WHERE measurand LIKE 'Energy.Active.%.Register')) AS kwh, max(value * CASE WHEN unit = 'kW' THEN 1 WHEN unit = 'MW' THEN 1000 ELSE 0.001 END) FILTER (WHERE measurand = 'Power.Active.Import') AS peak_kw, avg(value * CASE WHEN unit = 'kW' THEN 1 WHEN unit = 'MW' THEN 1000 ELSE 0.001 END) FILTER (WHERE measurand = 'Power.Active.Import') AS avg_kw, avg(value * CASE WHEN unit = 'kW' THEN 1 WHEN unit = 'MW' THEN 1000 ELSE 0.001 END) FILTER (WHERE measurand = 'Power.Active.Import' AND ts >= seg_end - interval '2 minutes') AS tail_kw, count(*) FILTER (WHERE measurand = 'Power.Active.Import') AS n_power, max(ts) > now() - interval '3 minutes' AS is_live FROM seg2 GROUP BY 1, 2, 3, 4), act AS (SELECT charge_point, connector_id, max(ts) AS last_any FROM meter_samples WHERE (CASE WHEN '$mode' = 'live' THEN NOT is_sim WHEN '$mode' = 'sim' THEN is_sim ELSE true END) GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT act.charge_point AS "charge point", CASE act.connector_id WHEN 1 THEN 'Gun A' WHEN 2 THEN 'Gun B' ELSE 'Conn ' || act.connector_id END AS "gun", act.last_any AS "last report", max(s.end_ts) AS "last session", count(s.start_ts) FILTER (WHERE $__timeFilter(s.start_ts))::int AS "sessions", round(sum(s.kwh) FILTER (WHERE $__timeFilter(s.start_ts))::numeric, 1) AS "kWh" FROM act LEFT JOIN sessions s USING (charge_point, connector_id) GROUP BY 1, act.connector_id, 3 ORDER BY 1, act.connector_id

panels.title: Buffer battery — charge per gun side
panels.description: State of charge of the charger’s internal buffer battery, per gun side, over the selected range. The battery-buffered signature: it dips while boosting a car beyond what the grid feed (~43 kW at the 63 A setting here) delivers, then refills slowly from the grid between sessions — a full recharge takes on the order of hours. Reported roughly every 15 minutes while the charger is connected; the line bridges gaps up to 45 minutes, longer gaps mean the charger was offline.

defaults.noValue: No buffer battery reports in range

targets.rawSql: SELECT time_bucket('1 minute', ts) AS "time", CASE connector_id WHEN 1 THEN 'Gun A side' WHEN 2 THEN 'Gun B side' ELSE 'Connector ' || connector_id END AS metric, avg(value) AS value FROM meter_samples WHERE (CASE WHEN '$mode' = 'live' THEN NOT is_sim WHEN '$mode' = 'sim' THEN is_sim ELSE true END) AND measurand = 'SoC' AND location = 'Body' AND $__timeFilter(ts) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Grid intake — derived from buffer physics
Grid draw while the buffer refills (est.)
panels.description: DERIVED ESTIMATE — the charger exposes no grid-side meter over OCPP, so grid intake is inferred from buffer-battery physics: the rise of the internal 218 kWh buffer's state of charge between two consecutive 15-minute reports × 218 kWh ÷ 15 min = the power the grid fed into the buffer. Guards: an interval only counts when both gun sides reported (a single side would skew the pack average), the two reports are strictly adjacent (no gap-spanning), and nothing in the interval belonged to a charging transaction or drew over 0.5 kW — and nothing is interpolated. Reading resolution: buffer SoC reports in ~0.5% steps, so each estimate quantizes to roughly ±4.4 kW, and any estimate above 90 kW — physically implausible for a 63 A feed, e.g. a firmware SoC recalibration jump — is dropped rather than shown. Cross-check: the measured ceiling (~43.6 kW) matches the unit's configured 63 A feed (√3 × 400 V × 63 A = 43.6 kW). Bars appear only for refill intervals; an empty stretch means the buffer was full or a car was charging. This is the effektavgift (demand-charge) story: the site never asks the grid for more than its small feed. Dashed grey line = the 43 kW (63 A) nominal feed.

targets.rawSql: WITH body AS (SELECT charge_point, time_bucket('15 minutes', ts) AS b, avg(value) AS soc FROM meter_samples WHERE (CASE WHEN '$mode' = 'live' THEN NOT is_sim WHEN '$mode' = 'sim' THEN is_sim ELSE true END) AND measurand = 'SoC' AND location = 'Body' AND $__timeFilter(ts) GROUP BY 1, 2 HAVING count(DISTINCT connector_id) >= 2), d AS (SELECT charge_point, b, soc, lag(b) OVER (PARTITION BY charge_point ORDER BY b) AS pb, lag(soc) OVER (PARTITION BY charge_point ORDER BY b) AS psoc FROM body), est AS (SELECT charge_point, b, (soc - psoc) / 100.0 * 218 / (EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (b - pb)) / 3600.0) AS est_kw FROM d WHERE pb IS NOT NULL AND b - pb = interval '15 minutes' AND soc > psoc AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM meter_samples p WHERE (CASE WHEN '$mode' = 'live' THEN NOT p.is_sim WHEN '$mode' = 'sim' THEN p.is_sim ELSE true END) AND p.charge_point = d.charge_point AND p.ts > d.pb AND p.ts <= d.b AND (p.transaction_id IS NOT NULL OR (p.measurand = 'Power.Active.Import' AND p.value * CASE WHEN p.unit = 'kW' THEN 1 WHEN p.unit = 'MW' THEN 1000 ELSE 0.001 END > 0.5)))) SELECT b AS "time", charge_point AS metric, round(est_kw::numeric, 1) AS value FROM est WHERE est_kw <= 90 ORDER BY b

panels.title: Peak grid draw (30 d, est.)
panels.description: DERIVED ESTIMATE — the charger exposes no grid-side meter over OCPP, so grid intake is inferred from buffer-battery physics: the rise of the internal 218 kWh buffer's state of charge between two consecutive 15-minute reports × 218 kWh ÷ 15 min = the power the grid fed into the buffer. Guards: an interval only counts when both gun sides reported (a single side would skew the pack average), the two reports are strictly adjacent (no gap-spanning), and nothing in the interval belonged to a charging transaction or drew over 0.5 kW — and nothing is interpolated. Reading resolution: buffer SoC reports in ~0.5% steps, so each estimate quantizes to roughly ±4.4 kW, and any estimate above 90 kW — physically implausible for a 63 A feed, e.g. a firmware SoC recalibration jump — is dropped rather than shown. Cross-check: the measured ceiling (~43.6 kW) matches the unit's configured 63 A feed (√3 × 400 V × 63 A = 43.6 kW). This 30-day peak is the number a demand charge would bill on. A conventional unbuffered 330 kW charger would need the grid to stand behind its full output instead.

targets.rawSql: WITH body AS (SELECT charge_point, time_bucket('15 minutes', ts) AS b, avg(value) AS soc FROM meter_samples WHERE (CASE WHEN '$mode' = 'live' THEN NOT is_sim WHEN '$mode' = 'sim' THEN is_sim ELSE true END) AND measurand = 'SoC' AND location = 'Body' AND ts > now() - interval '30 days' GROUP BY 1, 2 HAVING count(DISTINCT connector_id) >= 2), d AS (SELECT charge_point, b, soc, lag(b) OVER (PARTITION BY charge_point ORDER BY b) AS pb, lag(soc) OVER (PARTITION BY charge_point ORDER BY b) AS psoc FROM body), est AS (SELECT charge_point, b, (soc - psoc) / 100.0 * 218 / (EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (b - pb)) / 3600.0) AS est_kw FROM d WHERE pb IS NOT NULL AND b - pb = interval '15 minutes' AND soc > psoc AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM meter_samples p WHERE (CASE WHEN '$mode' = 'live' THEN NOT p.is_sim WHEN '$mode' = 'sim' THEN p.is_sim ELSE true END) AND p.charge_point = d.charge_point AND p.ts > d.pb AND p.ts <= d.b AND (p.transaction_id IS NOT NULL OR (p.measurand = 'Power.Active.Import' AND p.value * CASE WHEN p.unit = 'kW' THEN 1 WHEN p.unit = 'MW' THEN 1000 ELSE 0.001 END > 0.5)))) SELECT round(max(est_kw)::numeric, 1) AS "peak grid draw" FROM est WHERE est_kw <= 90
